title: Alkyl, Vinyl, Allyl and Aryl Halides: Which Carbon Holds X?
subject: Chemistry
objective: Alkyl, vinyl (vinylic), allyl (allylic) and aryl halides differ only in the carbon that holds the halogen. Alkyl: a saturated sp³ carbon (1°, 2°, 3° by the alkyl groups on it). Vinyl: X directly on a carbon of a C=C (sp²). Allyl: X on the sp³ carbon next to a C=C. Aryl: X directly on a carbon of an aromatic ring (sp²), e.g. chlorobenzene. Bonus: X on the sp³ CH₂ next to a benzene ring is a benzyl (benzylic) halide. Identify the carbon attached to X: that's the key.

fill.q: Monohalo compounds are classified by the hybridisation of the carbon bonded to the ____.
In an allylic halide, X is on an sp³ carbon next to a ____ double bond.
In a benzylic halide, X is on an sp³ carbon attached to a ____ ring.
In a vinylic halide, X is on an ____ carbon of a C=C.

tf.explain: Cl is one carbon away from the C=C: allylic.

tf.q: Benzyl chloride is an aryl halide.
tf.explain: Cl is on the CH₂ outside the ring: benzylic.

tf.q: In chlorobenzene the carbon bonded to Cl is sp².

tf.explain: Three alkyl groups on the C–Cl carbon.

ar.a: Assertion: CH₂=CHCH₂Cl is an allylic halide. Reason: Cl is bonded to an sp² carbon.
Assertion: Chlorobenzene needs 623 K and 300 atm to give phenol with NaOH. Reason: Its C–Cl bond is on an sp² carbon and is shorter and stronger.
ar.r: Both true; the reason explains the assertion.

mcq.explain: Br on the sp³ CH₂ attached to the ring.

short.q: Write the three steps to classify a monohalo compound.
short.solution: Find the carbon bonded to X; decide sp³ or sp²; look next door (C=C, ring or nothing).

short.q: Distinguish allylic and vinylic halides with an example each.
short.solution: Allylic: X on the sp³ C next to C=C (CH₂=CHCH₂Cl). Vinylic: X on a C=C carbon (CH₂=CHCl).

short.q: Distinguish benzylic and aryl halides with an example each.
short.solution: Benzylic: X on the sp³ C attached to a ring (C₆H₅CH₂Cl). Aryl: X directly on a ring carbon (C₆H₅Cl).
1-chloro: Cl on a C=C carbon, vinylic; 3-chloro: Cl next to the C=C, allylic.
